title: The explicit abelian Čech section augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U_i$ an open cover of $X$, and $F\to I^\bullet$ an injective resolution of an abelian sheaf [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The explicit restriction augmentation $\alpha:\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\to\mathrm{Tot}(\check C(U,I^\bullet))$ [def-pc-abelian-cech-comparison-construction] is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 20.11.2, quasi-isomorphism of alpha; Tag 0133, first-quadrant augmentation criterion

proof.text: Form the chain map a from the section complex to D.X 0 using restrictions; presheaf naturality proves its chain-map law, and the degree-zero Čech differential kills restrictions.
For each resolution degree form the single-zero augmentation into the corresponding Čech row. In positive Čech degrees apply the source injective Čech exactness theorem.

In Čech degree zero use the source gluing isomorphism. Transport cycles from the explicitly indexed short complex to the standard homology short complex, using the canonical isoSc map. Cancel the invertible homology projection to see that the lift to cycles is invertible.
Apply quasiIso_of_column_augmentation to a and the actual alpha map; its total-inclusion component identity is reflexivity. This yields QuasiIso alpha in Lean.
